title: Functional Groups (Alkyl Halides, Alcohols, Phenols, Aldehydes, & Ketones)
syllabus: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic substitution mechanisms (SN1 vs SN2 kinetics, stereochemistry, Walden inversion vs racemization, substrate reactivity, solvent and leaving group effects), elimination reactions (E1 and E2); Alcohols: Preparation, acidic character, distinction tests (Lucas test, Victor Meyer test), dehydration of alcohols (carbocation rearrangement, Zaitsev alkene formation), pinacol-pinacolone rearrangement; Phenols: Acidity, Kolbe's reaction, Reimer-Tiemann reaction (intermediate and mechanism), reaction with Zn dust, electrophilic substitutions (bromination, nitration); Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic addition reactions (addition of HCN, NaHSO3, Grignard reagents, alcohols, and ammonia derivatives), reactivity comparison toward nucleophilic attack; Alpha-hydrogen reactivity: Aldol condensation, cross-aldol condensation, Cannizzaro reaction and cross-Cannizzaro reaction, haloform test (iodoform reaction)

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] An optically active alkyl halide $(R)\text{-2-bromooctane}$ is reacted with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ under typical $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ conditions. The stereochemical outcome of the resulting octan-2-ol product is:
options: Complete inversion of configuration giving pure $(S)\text{-octan-2-ol}$
Complete retention of configuration giving pure $(R)\text{-octan-2-ol}$
Diastereomeric mixture with zero optical rotation
questions.solution:
1. Under classic bimolecular nucleophilic substitution $(\text{S}_\text{N}2)$ conditions, the incoming nucleophile $(\text{OH}^-)$ attacks the electrophilic carbon from the backside directly opposite to the leaving bromide group $(\text{Br}^-)$ in a single concerted step.
2. Backside attack forces the remaining three substituents to invert like an umbrella turned inside out in high winds (Walden inversion).
3. Since the relative priority ranking of groups remains unchanged $(-\text{OH}$ occupies the same priority rank as $-\text{Br})$, the $(R)$-enantiomer inverts completely into the $(S)$-enantiomer.
4. Therefore, $(R)\text{-2-bromooctane}$ yields exclusively **$(S)\text{-octan-2-ol}$ with complete stereochemical inversion**.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction of phenol with chloroform in the presence of aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: The reaction intermediate attacking the phenoxide ion is the trichloromethyl radical $(\dot{\text{C}}\text{Cl}_3)$
The electrophile is neutral dichlorocarbene $(:\text{CCl}_2)$ with an incomplete octet
The primary product after acidification is salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde)
The ortho-isomer predominates due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding in the intermediate and product
questions.solution:
Mechanism of the Reimer-Tiemann reaction:
1. Chloroform undergoes $\alpha$-elimination by $\text{OH}^-$:
$$\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{OH}^- \rightleftharpoons ^-\text{CCl}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{-\text{Cl}^-} :\text{CCl}_2$$
The active attacking electrophile is **neutral dichlorocarbene $(:\text{CCl}_2)$**, which has a vacant $p$-orbital and a lone pair in an $sp^2$ hybrid orbital. It is NOT a radical species.
2. The carbanion intermediate generated by electrophilic attack at the ortho position of phenoxide undergoes internal proton transfer and basic hydrolysis of the $-\text{CHCl}_2$ group to yield salicylaldehyde as the major product.
Therefore, Statement A is incorrect.

questions.question:
[JEE Main 2021] The correct decreasing order of reactivity toward nucleophilic addition reactions for the following carbonyl compounds is:
(I) $\text{HCHO}$
(II) $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$
(III) $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$
(IV) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$
questions.solution:
Reactivity toward nucleophilic addition is governed by:
- **Steric hindrance:** Smaller groups around the carbonyl carbon facilitate nucleophilic attack (Aldehydes > Ketones).
- **Electronic factors:** Electron-donating groups $(+I, +M)$ reduce the partial positive charge on the carbonyl carbon $(\,^{\delta+}\text{C}=\text{O}^{\delta-})$, decreasing reactivity.
1. $\text{HCHO}$ (Formaldehyde): Least sterically hindered and highest partial positive charge on carbon (no $+I$ groups) $\implies$ most reactive.
2. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ (Acetaldehyde): One methyl group $(+I)$ and minimal steric hindrance.
3. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$ (Benzaldehyde): The phenyl ring donates electron density into the carbonyl carbon via $+M$ resonance, diminishing its electrophilicity; however, as an aldehyde, it is still less sterically crowded than dialkyl ketones.
4. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ (Acetone): Two $+I$ electron-donating methyl groups reduce carbon electrophilicity and introduce steric hindrance.
Thus, the correct reactivity order is: (I) > (II) > (IV) > (III).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] An equimolar mixture of benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$) and formaldehyde ($\text{HCHO}$) is treated with concentrated aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ (Crossed Cannizzaro reaction). The products formed are:
questions.solution:
In the crossed Cannizzaro reaction between benzaldehyde and formaldehyde:
1. Neither aldehyde possesses any $\alpha$-hydrogens.
2. The initial rate-determining nucleophilic attack of hydroxide ion $(\text{OH}^-)$ occurs preferentially on the more electrophilic and sterically less hindered carbonyl carbon, which is formaldehyde $(\text{HCHO})$:
$$\text{HCHO} + \text{OH}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{C}(\text{OH})\text{O}^- \quad (\text{hydrated dianion/monoanion})$$
3. This tetrahedral species transfers a hydride ion $(\text{H}^-)$ to the less reactive benzaldehyde molecule:
$$\text{H}_2\text{C}(\text{O}^-)\text{OH} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{HCOOH} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{O}^-$$
4. Rapid proton transfer yields **sodium formate ($\text{HCOONa}$)** and **benzyl alcohol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$)**.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] When 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol is heated with concentrated sulfuric acid at $440\text{ K}$, the major alkene obtained is:
questions.solution:
Mechanism of acid-catalyzed dehydration of 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol:
1. Protonation followed by loss of water yields a secondary carbocation:
$$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+, -\text{H}_2\text{O}} (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}_3 \quad (2^\circ\text{ carbocation})$$
2. The adjacent carbon C-3 has three methyl groups. A rapid **1,2-methyl shift** occurs to relieve steric crowding and generate a far more stable tertiary carbocation:
$$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{1,2-\text{Me shift}} (\text{CH}_3)_2\overset{+}{\text{C}}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \quad (3^\circ\text{ carbocation})$$
3. Loss of a proton according to Zaitsev's rule yields the most highly substituted, tetrasubstituted alkene (having $12\ \alpha$-hydrogens):
$$(\text{CH}_3)_2\overset{+}{\text{C}}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{-\text{H}^+} (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2$$
This is **2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene (tetramethylethylene)**.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The Lucas test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols. The reagent used and the observation for a tertiary alcohol are:
options: Anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2 + \text{conc. HCl}$; turbidity appears immediately at room temperature
Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3 + \text{conc. HCl}$; turbidity appears after 5 minutes
Anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2 + \text{conc. HCl}$; solution remains clear upon heating
questions.solution:
1. Lucas reagent consists of an equimolar mixture of **anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$ and concentrated $\text{HCl}$**.
2. The reaction proceeds via an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism involving the formation of an intermediate carbocation:
$$\text{R}-\text{OH} + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{ZnCl}_2} \text{R}-\text{Cl} \downarrow \text{ (turbidity)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
3. The rate of carbocation formation determines the rate of appearance of insoluble alkyl chloride (turbidity):
- **$3^\circ$ alcohols:** Form very stable tertiary carbocations; turbidity appears **immediately** at room temperature.
- **$2^\circ$ alcohols:** Turbidity appears within $5-10\text{ minutes}$.
- **$1^\circ$ alcohols:** Do not form turbidity at room temperature; turbidity appears only upon vigorous heating.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Which of the following compounds will NOT undergo an aldol condensation when treated with dilute aqueous $\text{NaOH}$?
questions.solution:
Aldol condensation requires the presence of at least one acidic **$\alpha$-hydrogen** atom attached to an $sp^3$ carbon adjacent to the carbonyl group to generate an enolate nucleophile:
1. Ethanal $(\text{CH}_3\text{CHO})$: Has $3\ \alpha$-hydrogens $\implies$ undergoes aldol.
2. Propanal $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO})$: Has $2\ \alpha$-hydrogens $\implies$ undergoes aldol.
3. Propan-2-one $(\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3)$: Has $6\ \alpha$-hydrogens $\implies$ undergoes aldol.
4. 2,2-Dimethylpropanal $((\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CHO})$: The $\alpha$-carbon is quaternary and bonded to three methyl groups, possessing **zero $\alpha$-hydrogens**. Instead of aldol condensation, it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction in the presence of concentrated base.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following alkyl halides undergoes nucleophilic substitution by an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway at the FASTEST rate?
questions.solution:
The rate of an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction is determined by the thermodynamic stability of the intermediate carbocation generated during the rate-limiting heterolysis of the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond:
1. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}(\text{Cl})-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$: Ionization produces the diphenylmethyl cation, $(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_2\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}$, where the positive charge is delocalized over **two aromatic benzene rings** (extensive resonance stabilization across $7$ canonical contributors).
2. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$: Benzyl cation is stabilized by one aromatic ring.
3. $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{Cl}$: tert-Butyl cation is stabilized by $9\ \alpha$-hydrogens via hyperconjugation.
4. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$: Primary alkyl cation is unstable.
Because the diphenylmethyl carbocation is stabilized by two conjugated phenyl rings, its precursor hydrolyzes at the fastest rate via $\text{S}_\text{N}1$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] When phenol is distilled with zinc dust, the product obtained is:
questions.solution:
Distillation of phenol with zinc dust causes reduction of the phenolic hydroxyl group:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{Zn} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{ZnO}$$
1. Zinc acts as a reducing agent, removing the oxygen atom to form zinc oxide ($\text{ZnO}$).
2. The aromatic ring is deoxygenated, producing **benzene** in high yield.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Which of the following compounds gives a POSITIVE iodoform test (formation of yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ upon treatment with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$)?
questions.solution:
The iodoform test gives a positive result for compounds containing either:
- A methyl carbonyl group: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{R}$
- A secondary methyl carbinol group that oxidizes to a methyl ketone: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{R}$ (or ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$)
Evaluate the options:
1. Pentan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$): Contains a $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-$ group $\implies$ forms yellow $\text{CHI}_3 \downarrow$.
2. Pentan-3-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$): Contains an ethyl ketone group with no terminal methyl attached to the carbonyl $\implies$ negative.
3. Benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$): No $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-$ group $\implies$ negative.
4. Methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$): Cannot be oxidized to a methyl ketone $\implies$ negative.
Thus, pentan-2-one gives a positive iodoform test.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] In the Kolbe's reaction, sodium phenoxide is heated with carbon dioxide at $400\text{ K}$ under $4-7\text{ atm}$ pressure, followed by acidification to produce:
options: p-Hydroxybenzoic acid as the exclusive product
questions.solution:
In Kolbe-Schmitt reaction:
1. The phenoxide ion ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}^-$) has high electron density due to the strong $+M$ resonance donation of the oxide oxygen.
2. It attacks the weak electrophile carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) at the ortho position:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{ONa} + \text{CO}_2 \xrightarrow{400\text{ K}, 4-7\text{ atm}} \text{o-HOC}_6\text{H}_4\text{COONa}$$
3. Acidification with mineral acid yields **salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid)** as the major product, stabilized by an intramolecular hydrogen bond.

questions.question: For the solvolysis of $(R)\text{-1-phenylethyl chloride}$ in aqueous acetone via an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism, the optical activity of the resulting alcohol product mixture shows:
options: Partial racemization accompanied by net inversion of configuration
Complete $100\%$ racemization with zero optical activity
questions.solution:
In an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ process:
1. The departing leaving group ($\text{Cl}^-$) initially forms an **intimate ion pair** $[\text{R}^+\cdots\text{Cl}^-]$ before fully diffusing away.
2. The leaving group temporarily shields the front face from which it departed.
3. The nucleophile (water) preferentially attacks the unhindered back face, leading to a higher proportion of inverted product.
4. Attack from the front face occurs once the leaving group diffuses away, producing the retained enantiomer.
Consequently, typical $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reactions at a chiral carbon show **partial racemization with a net excess of inversion of configuration**.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Addition of hydrogen cyanide ($\text{HCN}$) to an aldehyde or ketone in the presence of a catalytic amount of base is an example of:
options: Nucleophilic addition initiated by the attack of cyanide ion
Electrophilic addition initiated by the attack of proton
Nucleophilic substitution with loss of oxygen
questions.solution:
1. $\text{HCN}$ is a weak acid and ionizes slowly in pure water. A catalytic base ($\text{OH}^-$) generates the strong nucleophile cyanide ion ($\text{CN}^-$):
$$\text{HCN} + \text{OH}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{CN}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
2. Rate-determining step: The nucleophilic $\text{CN}^-$ attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon to form a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate:
$$\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{O} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C}(\text{CN})\text{O}^-$$
3. Protonation by $\text{HCN}$ regenerates the catalyst $\text{CN}^-$ and yields the cyanohydrin product:
$$\text{R}_2\text{C}(\text{CN})\text{O}^- + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C}(\text{OH})\text{CN} + \text{CN}^-$$
This is a classic **nucleophilic addition reaction**.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] When phenol is treated with excess bromine water, it produces an immediate white precipitate of:
questions.solution:
1. In aqueous medium (polar protic solvent), phenol undergoes extensive ionization to form the phenoxide ion ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}^-$).
2. The negative charge on oxygen dramatically amplifies $+M$ electron donation into the aromatic ring, strongly activating all ortho and para positions toward electrophilic substitution.
3. Even without a Lewis acid catalyst, bromine water rapidly brominates all available ortho and para positions:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 3\text{Br}_2(aq) \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_2\text{Br}_3\text{OH} \downarrow + 3\text{HBr}$$
This produces a white precipitate of **2,4,6-tribromophenol**.
(In non-polar solvents like $\text{CS}_2$ or $\text{CHCl}_3$ at low temperatures, ionization is suppressed and monobromophenol is obtained).

questions.question:
[JEE Main 2022] In the self-aldol condensation of acetaldehyde followed by heating with acid:
$$2\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. NaOH}} A \xrightarrow{\Delta, \text{H}^+} B$$
The final dehydrated product $B$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Base deprotonates acetaldehyde to form the enolate ion, which nucleophilically attacks a second molecule of acetaldehyde to yield 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol intermediate $A$):
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{CH}_2^-\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{O}^-)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$$
2. Upon heating under acidic conditions, the aldol intermediate undergoes dehydration (E1cB or E2 elimination) to eliminate water and generate a stable conjugated $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated aldehyde:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\Delta, -\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CHO}$$
Product $B$ is **but-2-enal (crotonaldehyde)**.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Which of the following solvents promotes the $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism at the HIGHEST rate?
questions.solution:
1. In an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism, the rate-determining transition state involves nucleophilic attack without preliminary carbocation generation:
$$\text{Rate} = k[\text{Substrate}][\text{Nucleophile}]$$
2. **Polar protic solvents** (like water, ethanol, acetic acid) engage in strong hydrogen bonding with the anionic nucleophile, creating a solvent cage that deactivates the nucleophile and lowers the reaction rate.
3. **Polar aprotic solvents** (like DMSO, DMF, acetone, acetonitrile) solvate cations effectively through dipole interactions, leaving the anionic nucleophile unsolvated ("naked") and highly reactive.
Consequently, $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactions proceed most rapidly in polar aprotic solvents like **DMSO**.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] An organic compound $X$ on treatment with hydrazine ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$) followed by heating with $\text{KOH}$ in ethylene glycol produces propane. Compound $X$ can be:
questions.solution:
The reaction sequence describes the **Wolff-Kishner reduction**:
$$\text{C}=\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2, \text{KOH}, \text{glycol}, \Delta} \text{CH}_2 + \text{N}_2 \uparrow$$
1. The Wolff-Kishner reduction selectively reduces the carbonyl group ($-\text{C}=\text{O}$) of aldehydes and ketones into a methylene group ($-\text{CH}_2-$).
2. Propane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$) has 3 carbon atoms.
3. Reducing propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$) or acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) converts the $\text{C}=\text{O}$ group to $-\text{CH}_2-$, yielding propane:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
Thus, compound $X$ can be either propanal or propan-2-one.

questions.question: The primary reason 2-methylpropan-2-ol (tert-butanol) does NOT undergo oxidation with acidified sodium dichromate at room temperature is:
options: The carbinol carbon atom lacks an $\alpha$-hydrogen atom
Tertiary alcohols are insoluble in acidic aqueous solutions
The hydroxyl oxygen is protonated irreversibly
Tertiary alcohols undergo reduction instead of oxidation
questions.solution:
1. The oxidation of an alcohol to a carbonyl compound by chromic acid involves initial formation of a chromate ester followed by base-assisted elimination of a proton from the **carbinol carbon** (the carbon bearing the $-\text{OH}$ group, requiring an $\alpha$-hydrogen):
$$\text{R}_2\text{CH}-\text{OH} \xrightarrow{[\text{O}]} \text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{O} + 2\text{H}^+ + 2e^-$$
2. In tert-butanol, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{OH}$, the carbinol carbon is bonded to three methyl groups and has **no $\alpha$-hydrogen**.
3. Because there is no hydrogen to eliminate, oxidation cannot proceed under mild conditions (vigorous conditions cause dehydration followed by oxidative cleavage of $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bonds).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The reaction of an aldehyde with a primary amine in the presence of an acid catalyst produces:
questions.solution:
Reaction of aldehydes/ketones with primary aliphatic or aromatic amines:
$$\text{R}-\text{CHO} + \text{R}'-\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} [\text{R}-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{NHR}'] \xrightarrow{-\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{R}-\text{CH}=\text{N}-\text{R}'$$
1. Nucleophilic addition of the amine lone pair forms an unstable carbinolamine intermediate.
2. Subsequent acid-catalyzed dehydration eliminates water to form a carbon-nitrogen double bond compound (an **imine**, commonly referred to as a **Schiff base**).
(In contrast, secondary amines yield enamines, while hydroxylamine yields oximes).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In which of the following pairs of reactions does the first reaction proceed via an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism and the second via an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism?
questions.solution:
1. $\text{CH}_3\text{Br} + \text{OH}^-$:
- Methyl halide has minimal steric hindrance, leaving the electrophilic carbon fully exposed to backside attack.
- Strong nucleophile $(\text{OH}^-)$ favors a bimolecular pathway.
- Proceeds via an **$\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism**.
2. $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{Br} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$:
- Tertiary substrate is sterically hindered, preventing backside approach of nucleophiles.
- Ionization produces a tertiary carbocation, and water acts as a weak nucleophile in a polar protic medium.
- Proceeds via an **$\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism**.
Thus, Option A correctly matches.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] In the complete Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde, how many moles of benzoic acid (or sodium benzoate) are formed from $2\text{ moles}$ of benzaldehyde?
questions.solution:
The disproportionation stoichiometry of the Cannizzaro reaction is:
$$2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
- $1\text{ mole}$ of benzaldehyde is reduced to benzyl alcohol.
- $1\text{ mole}$ of benzaldehyde is oxidized to sodium benzoate (which yields benzoic acid upon acidification).
Therefore, exactly $1.0\text{ mole}$ of benzoic acid is formed from $2\text{ moles}$ of benzaldehyde.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Find the total number of structural (constitutional) aldol addition products possible from the crossed aldol reaction between an equimolar mixture of ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) and propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$).
questions.solution:
Both ethanal and propanal possess acidic $\alpha$-hydrogens and can act as both enolate donors and electrophilic carbonyl acceptors:
1. Self-aldol of ethanal: enolate of ethanal attacks ethanal $\implies$ 3-hydroxybutanal
2. Self-aldol of propanal: enolate of propanal attacks propanal $\implies$ 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal
3. Crossed aldol 1: enolate of ethanal attacks propanal $\implies$ 3-hydroxypentanal
4. Crossed aldol 2: enolate of propanal attacks ethanal $\implies$ 3-hydroxy-2-methylbutanal
Total number of structural aldol addition products $= 4.0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Find the total number of $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms present in one molecule of propan-2-one (acetone).
questions.solution:
Structure of propan-2-one:
$$\overset{\alpha}{\text{C}}\text{H}_3-\text{CO}-\overset{\alpha'}{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$$
- The carbonyl group is flanked by two methyl groups.
- Each methyl carbon is in the $\alpha$-position and possesses three hydrogen atoms.
$$\text{Total } \alpha\text{-hydrogens} = 3 + 3 = 6.0$$

questions.question:
[JEE Main 2023] In the iodoform reaction of acetone:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 \downarrow + \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + 3\text{NaI} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Calculate the number of moles of $\text{I}_2$ consumed per mole of acetone.
questions.solution:
From the balanced stoichiometry of the haloform reaction:
- Three $\alpha$-hydrogens on the methyl group are sequentially replaced by three iodine atoms via electrophilic iodination of the enolate to form a triiodo intermediate ($\text{CI}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$):
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 3\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CI}_3\text{COCH}_3 + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
- The fourth hydroxide ion cleaves the $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond to release $\text{CHI}_3$ and acetate:
$$\text{CI}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$$
Hence, exactly $3.0\text{ moles of } \text{I}_2$ are consumed per mole of acetone.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Among the following organic compounds: methanol, ethanol, propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol, butan-1-ol, pentan-2-one, pentan-3-one, and acetophenone, how many give a POSITIVE iodoform test?
questions.solution:
Evaluate for the structural requirement of a positive iodoform test (presence of $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-$ or $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-$):
1. Methanol: $\text{CH}_3\text{OH} \implies$ Negative
2. Ethanol: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (oxidizes to $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) $\implies$ Positive
3. Propan-1-ol: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \implies$ Negative
4. Propan-2-ol: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3$ (has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$) $\implies$ Positive
5. Butan-1-ol: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \implies$ Negative
6. Pentan-2-one: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (has $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$) $\implies$ Positive
7. Pentan-3-one: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \implies$ Negative
8. Acetophenone: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$ (has $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$) $\implies$ Positive
Total compounds giving a positive test $= 4.0$ (ethanol, propan-2-ol, pentan-2-one, acetophenone).
